newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares strong on rouble news.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares strong on rouble news.

text.p: A report that a tender for 38 percent of Russia's Norilsk Nickel might be suspended came too late in the afternoon to affect most shares, which firmed on Monday to close up on mixed buying orders, traders said.
But they were unsure of how the Norilsk report, if confirmed, might affect the market on Tuesday.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index finished up at 518.31 after closing on Friday at 510.20. Total market turnover was an average $55.3 million.
Traders attributed the uptick, which came after a sluggish morning session, to news the government would introduce a new rouble, worth 1,000 old ones, on January 1, 1998.
"Some local, but fairly big, orders came in, which I associate with the announcement today of the rouble denomination," said ING Bank trader Oleg Galkin.
"The denomination confirms a stable economy overall: if people are doing that it means things aren't so bad."
National power company UES rose to $0.4305 from Friday's closing $0.4240 and oil company LUKoil firmed to $23.25 after $22.93.

United Financial Group trader Maxim Perlin said oil company Surgutneftegaz at $1.25 and regional telecom Uralsvyazinform at $0.069 both reached historical highs and saw the market consolidating at a new level.

But preferred shares in metal producer Norilsk fell -- to $12.40 from $13.40 at 1341 GMT and $13.50 at Friday's close -- in the last 20 minutes of trading following an unconfirmed report that Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had ordered the tender suspended.
Previously officials had said preferred shares would be convertible to more valuable ordinary shares after the sale.
"It's difficlt to say how it will affect the market if the information is confirmed," said a trader at Alfa Capital.
"The behaviour of Norilsk shares will depend on what position the main players -- those who have been active in the stock recently -- take tomorrow."
